parole.significato: amen, so be it (at the end of a religious prayer)
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Dutch amen, from Latin āmēn, from Ancient Greek ἀμήν (amḗn), from Biblical Hebrew אמן (amén, “certainly, truly”).
Borrowed from Ecclesiastical Latin blasphēmia, from Ancient Greek βλασφημία (blasphēmía, “profanity”), from βλασφημέω (blasphēméō, “to slander”).

parole.significato: a dalmatic, notably as Catholic liturgic vestment
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch dalmatike, from Ecclesiastical Latin dalmatica, from the feminine of Dalmaticus (“Dalmatian”), from Dalmatia; cognate with French dalmatique, German Dalmatika etc.

parole.significato: deacon (person involved in an ecclesiastical lay office for social affairs and charity)
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Dutch diaken, from Ecclesiastical Latin diāconus, from Ancient Greek διᾱ́κονος (diā́konos, “servant, minister”).
Ultimately from Ecclesiastical Latin eucharisticus. Equivalent to eucharistie + -isch.
From Middle Dutch heremite, heremijt and eremijt, a borrowing from Ecclesiastical Latin erēmīta, borrowed from Ancient Greek ἐρημίτης (erēmítēs).

parole.significato: a canon, a cleric subject to an ecclesiastical rule
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch canonec, from Ecclesiastical Latin canonicus, from Ancient Greek κανονικός (kanonikós).
